correctness.rationale: Conditional on a specified isolated vertex in G(n,m), all m edges are uniform on n-1 vertices; because motif H has no isolated vertices, every motif copy avoids that vertex. The ratio of conditional to unconditional E[X_H] is (n-v)/n*(N)_e/(P)_e, producing the claimed covariance factor for e<=m<=P with positive means. For m<e or m>P one variable is identically zero. Independent-edge G(n,p) leaves all other edges independent and yields negative -v/n factor. For trees, exact adjacent ratio and n=7 rational values (1,8/7,114/91,114/91,969/1001) checked; unimodality, final <1 for n>=7, and log R→log(1−alpha)+2alpha establish unique finite and asymptotic sign transitions. Finite checks corroborate, not replace, conditional counting and analytic bounds.

value.rationale: This gives a complete exact sign classification independent of the edge count and tree shape, with a sharp macroscopic tree-size threshold reversing the G(n,p) sign. The observable pair (isolates, motif embeddings) is standard in random graphs and a uniform model-dependent covariance phase transition is a natural precise statistic to know.

limitations: Applies to non-induced H without isolated vertices, positive-overlap edge-count range; not induced motif covariance or critical asymptotic line alpha=alpha_*.
